MA342 overview

MA342 Topic Guide

Homotopy and Simply Connected Spaces

Make deformation arguments explicit through a continuous parameter.

Purpose

State a homotopy precisely and exploit convex codomains to construct it by linear interpolation; keep contractions and simple connectedness as related secondary material.Exam use: The 2025/26 Q4(e) allocates 6 marks to the definition and to proving that arbitrary continuous maps Rn→Rn are homotopic.

Question plan

  1. Identify the two maps f,g:X→Y.
  2. Give H:X×[0,1]→Y with H(x,0)=f(x), H(x,1)=g(x).
  3. Check H remains in Y and is continuous; convexity is the key codomain property for linear interpolation.
  4. Question interpretation: “Define homotopic” needs the domain, codomain and both endpoint equations; “show homotopic” needs an explicit H plus continuity and codomain checks.

Definitions

Continuous maps f,g:X→Y are homotopic if there is a continuous H:X×[0,1]→Y satisfying H(x,0)=f(x) and H(x,1)=g(x) for every x∈X. A contraction is a homotopy from idX to a constant map. X is simply connected if it is path connected and every loop is homotopic to a constant loop.Rapid recall: Write H’s full type, continuity, both endpoint maps and why every intermediate value lies in Y.

Proof method

For f,g:X→Rn, use H(x,t)=(1−t)f(x)+tg(x). The vector-space operations and continuity of f,g make H continuous, and convexity of Rn keeps the entire line segment in the codomain.Exam workflow: Write the interpolation, check t=0 and t=1, cite continuity of sums and scalar products, and name convexity when the codomain is a proper subset.

Worked simple example

R² is contractible: H(x,t)=(1−t)x deforms the identity to the constant map at 0.

Medium/hard paper-style synthesis

Let f,g:Rn→Rn be continuous. Define H(x,t)=(1−t)f(x)+tg(x). Then H(x,0)=f(x) and H(x,1)=g(x). The formula is continuous as a combination of continuous maps, and every value is in Rn. Hence f and g are homotopic.

Graduated exam bridges

1. Foundation: Show any two constant maps X→R are homotopic. Check: linearly interpolate their values and verify both endpoints.

2. Exam style: Generalise the paper argument to maps f,g:X→C where C⊆Rn is convex. Check: the segment between f(x) and g(x) remains in C.

Hard paper-style synthesis

Convexity is sufficient but not necessary for two maps to be homotopic. The straight-line formula can fail for a non-convex codomain: interpolating two points of S1 generally passes through the disk rather than staying on the circle. A valid formula must land in the declared codomain for every (x,t).

Practice question - arbitrary maps into Rn [6 marks]

Inspired by: MA342 2025/26 Q4(e). Task. (a) Define what it means for continuous maps f,g:X→Y to be homotopic. (b) Let f,g:Rn→Rn be continuous. Show that f and g are homotopic. [6 marks]

Demand diagnosis and fastest route: give the complete definition, then use straight-line interpolation in the convex codomain Rn.

Worked answer: The maps f and g are homotopic if a continuous H:X×[0,1]→Y exists such that H(x,0)=f(x) and H(x,1)=g(x) for all x∈X. For maps Rn→Rn, define H(x,t)=(1−t)f(x)+tg(x). This map is continuous because f and g are continuous and vector addition and scalar multiplication are continuous. Moreover H(x,t)∈Rn for every x and t, while H(x,0)=f(x) and H(x,1)=g(x). Thus f and g are homotopic.

Topic-specific trap: do not use H(x,t)=(1−t)x unless f is the identity and g is the zero map; the paper asks about arbitrary f and g.

Mistakes

  • Giving a family H without endpoint checks.
  • Failing to prove H takes values in the target space.
  • Calling a connected space simply connected without addressing loops.
  • Recovery rule: A formula that leaves the space is not a homotopy in that space; verify the codomain condition for every t.

Checklist

  • I can write the domain and endpoint equations of H.
  • I can interpolate arbitrary maps into Rn.
  • I can contract a star-shaped set.
  • I know S¹ is connected but not simply connected.
  • Final 60-second audit: Formula, continuity, image containment, endpoint maps and base/path conditions appear.

Past-paper note

High confidence for homotopy: homotopy appears in all three papers from 2023/24 through 2025/26. The new Q4(e) fixes the current 6-mark family as the exact definition plus straight-line homotopy between arbitrary continuous maps Rn→Rn. Simply connected/star-shaped work remains secondary evidence from 2023/24. Back to paper evidence.
